subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - FinLytics
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily@finlytics.com>, Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv.malhotra@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - FinLytics

Hi Emily / Rajiv,

Thanks again for the time today — good call. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size a dedicated proposal that matches FinLytics' needs. Please confirm the bullets below and let me know if anything's off.

Summary from the call:
- Target workloads: real-time document enrichment + batch nightly reindexing (mix of chat+generation + embeddings).
- Estimated monthly token volume range: 200M - 1B tokens/month (you indicated scaling to ~1B in peak months).
- Latency SLO: sub-300ms 95p for interactive annotator flows; nightly batch tolerant of higher latency.
- Preferred model family: mix of Llama/Redwood-verified open models for chat + local embedding models.

Pricing / unit-economics goal (from your team):
- Target unit cost: $500 - $800 per 1M tokens (desired range).
- Target committed budget range: $40k - $120k / month (goal to land in this band for reserved capacity).

Sizing assumptions we want to validate:
- Average request size: 600 tokens (interactive), batch avg 1,500 tokens per document (we used weighted average to build throughput).
- Concurrency target for interactive flows: 40 concurrent sessions during peak.
- Throughput target (sustained): ~15k - 30k tokens/sec depending on model/quality/quantization.

Dedicated capacity options we discussed (rough):
- 4x A100 (40GB) — good for small-medium workloads; estimated throughput ~10k-15k tokens/sec for our reference models; lower cost than H100.
- 4x H100 (80GB) — better latency and higher sustained throughput; recommended for tighter latency SLOs at scale.
- 8x A100 — a mid-point if you want headroom for growth without moving to H100.

Questions / asks (next steps):
1) Can you confirm the expected monthly token volume you want to commit to for the first 6 months (pick a point in the 200M-1B range)?
2) Do you have a strong preference for A100 vs H100 (we can price both; H100 typically reduces latency and gives better headroom for large context/kv cache).
3) Any procurement timelines or PO windows we should be aware of?

I've attached a short mutual action plan template and a pricing estimate workbook; I'll follow up with a more formal quote once you confirm the above.

Attachments: FinLytics_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx, pricing_estimate.xlsx

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Chen <emily@finlytics.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv.malhotra@finlytics.com>, FinLytics Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T18:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification - FinLytics

Thanks, Dylan — great summary. A few clarifications from our side:

Confirmed:
- Committed monthly volume to start: 400M tokens/month (we anticipate hitting 1B after 3-4 quarters).
- Target unit cost: ideally <$700 / 1M tokens; open to discussion based on SLA and model mix.

Preference:
- We're leaning toward H100 for the initial reserved pool because of latency concerns for the annotator UI and the larger context sizes we'll use.

Procurement / timeline:
- Procurement intends to sign a 12-month reserved commitment if pricing and SLA are acceptable.
- Decision target: end of May (we have a board review in early June).

Two additional asks:
1) Can you include estimated network egress and storage cost assumptions in the workbook? (We need numbers for our finance model.)
2) We need a short tech deep-dive to validate throughput assumptions with our engineering team — can Marcus join that?

–Emily
Emily Chen
Head of ML Platforms | FinLytics

Thanks Emily — that's super helpful. Quick response to your asks and next steps:

What we'll add to the workbook (attached):
- Estimated reserved capacity monthly price for both A100 and H100 options (list price + committed discount scenarios).
- Unit cost ($ / 1M tokens) derived from reserved capacity + expected utilization assumptions.
- Separate line items for egress (estimated $/GB) and storage (GB of model weights + persistent cache).

High-level pricing examples (initial, illustrative — final quote to follow):
- 4x H100 reserved pool — estimated list cost (after baseline discounts) ~ $90k / month.
  - Assumes sustained throughput ~25k tokens/sec for our reference model mix; maps to ~$225 / 1M tokens at 400M tokens/month utilization (note: this is illustrative and sensitive to utilization and model choice).
- 4x A100 reserved pool — estimated list cost ~ $55k / month.
  - Assumes sustained throughput ~12k tokens/sec; maps to ~$275 / 1M tokens at 400M tokens/month (again, illustrative).

Notes on assumptions:
- Unit $/1M tokens shown above assumes ~60-70% sustained utilization of the reserved pool across peak/batch mix. If utilization is lower the unit cost rises; higher utilization drives the unit cost down.
- We include burst capacity options (metered) to handle short spikes; burst usage is billed separately.

Attachments: FinLytics_MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN.xlsx, Redwood_SOW_v1.pdf, pricing_estimate.xlsx

Next steps
- I'll schedule a technical deep-dive this week with Marcus to validate throughput numbers (Marcus — are you available Thu or Fri PST?).
- Emily / Rajiv — if you can confirm the 400M monthly commit as your starting point, we'll produce a formal reserved-capacity quote and a draft SOW for procurement.

Thanks —
Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Emily / team — quick technical note following up from Dylan's sizing estimates. High level guidance for the throughput targets you listed:

- For ~400M tokens/month and target interactive latency (<300ms 95p) with average request size ~600 tokens and ~40 concurrent sessions, we recommend starting with 6x H100 (80GB) reserved. That gives sustained throughput headroom ~20k-30k tokens/sec depending on model quantization and batching settings.
- If you prefer A100 (cost-driven), 8-10x A100 (40GB) would be the comparable alternative to hit similar sustained throughput with slightly higher latency on 95p.
- We will validate these with an in-house benchmark using your representative prompt set and the exact models you plan to run; if you can share sample prompt sets and average context sizes we can run a 48-72 hour workload test.

I'll be available for the deep-dive Thu 4/22 10:00-11:30 PST or Fri 4/23 13:00-15:00 PST. Let me know which works and we'll send a calendar invite + shared benchmark doc.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
